subject: Regional pin certification and procedural egress approval
messages:
From: Claremont Health <security@claremonthealth.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: DPA-Legal <legal@claremonthealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Regional residency confirmation needed for onboarding

Hi Sergio,

As part of our onboarding checklist we need a written confirmation of the following items before we complete procurement:

1) A firm statement of where PII-derived embeddings and full request logs are stored (primary region) for the CLM-0423 workload.
2) Commitment window for region pinning (how long data remains pinned to the US region vs. allowed transient hops).
3) For transient cross-region processing (e.g., analytics or batch reindexing), a description of the approval workflow and maximum permitted dwell time.
4) A roster of subprocessors that might process data outside the US and the activation conditions that trigger cross-region hops.

We prefer short, operational language — our compliance team will use this to complete our DPA checklist. If you have a runbook or short playbook that describes the operational steps for temporary egress, please attach it.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Security Operations
Claremont Health

[Attachment: onboarding-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Claremont Health <security@claremonthealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional residency confirmation needed for onboarding

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I’ll loop in Legal (Marissa) and Ops (Kimberly) for runbook detail and the subprocessor roster.

1) Primary storage: All request logs and PII-derived embeddings for the CLM-0423 tenant are stored in the US region (us-central-1) by default. We persist both the raw request metadata and embeddings in that region unless a pin for another region is requested.

2) Pinning commitment: We support explicit region pinning with a contractual commitment of 12 months by default. We also support shorter pinned windows for pilots; we can document a 30/90/365-day selection in the SOW.

3) Transient cross-region processing: Temporary hops are allowed under a documented approval flow. Typical permitted dwell time for analytics-style transient processing is up to 72 hours (48–72h typical), with automated TTL-based cache purges and audit logs. Any dwell time >72h requires executive approval and a DPA addendum.

4) Subprocessors: We have a small set of analytics and telemetry subprocessors that may require cross-region processing under strict conditions. Marissa will provide the roster + activation conditions.

I’m attaching a light operational runbook that covers the approval flow, KMS handling, and audit evidence we provide. Kimberly: can you confirm the KMS key residency and the default telemetry masking applied during transient hops?

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Head of North America Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-pin-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, Claremont Health <security@claremonthealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-18T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional residency confirmation needed for onboarding

Hi Elena,

Following up with the legal/controls detail you asked for and the subprocessor roster. Please find the key items below and the roster attached.

- Subprocessor roster (attached): includes processors that may be invoked for batch analytics (e.g., analytics-ops partner) and their activation triggers (scheduled reindexing, emergency capacity failover, or customer-authorized forensic analysis).
- Activation conditions: cross-region processing is only initiated when (a) a named trigger in the SOW occurs, (b) a documented temporary-egress form is submitted and approved by Redwoods Ops, or (c) an ops-critical failover is invoked under our SLA failover policy. We never proactively move customer data without explicit approval or documented SLO-triggered failover.
- KMS & key control: Customer data at rest remains encrypted using keys resident in the pinned region. For transient processing where data must be decrypted outside the primary region, we employ a short-lived re-encryption key issued by our KMS and logged in the audit trail. Keys for egressed jobs are never exported; they are ephemeral and restricted to the job lifecycle.
- Auditability: Every transient hop is logged with request IDs, job run timestamps, and the approving ticket. Audit logs are retained per the DPA terms and are available in our Console tracing for the account.

See attached: subprocessor-activation-roster.csv and an example temporary egress form (claremont-temp-egress-form.pdf).

If you want, we can add a one-paragraph DPA addendum clause to codify the 72-hour transient threshold and the exec-approval path for anything longer. If Claremont signs that, it avoids repeated exec approvals for future scheduled analytics windows.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: subprocessor-activation-roster.csv (csv), claremont-temp-egress-form.pdf (pdf)]

From: Claremont Health <security@claremonthealth.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: DPA-Legal <legal@claremonthealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional residency confirmation needed for onboarding

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. Two follow-ups before we finalize:

- For scheduled analytics runs that fall into the 48–72h window, do you provide an automated notification and a pre-signed acknowledgement where we can see the exact list of subprocessor IDs and the job run window? We’d like automated transparency rather than relying on ad-hoc tickets.
- For emergency failover that could require >72h processing in another region, can you commit to a documented escrow path or compensating control (e.g., encrypted snapshot escrow held in a jurisdiction we approve) while exec-approval is obtained?

If you can provide the notification automation and a short escrow/control paragraph we can insert into the DPA, we’ll be comfortable moving to signature.

Elena Martinez
Head of Security Operations
Claremont Health

From: sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Claremont Health <security@claremonthealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-20T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional residency confirmation needed for onboarding

Elena — quick notes and next steps:

1) Automated notifications: Yes — we can enable an account-level notification feed that posts a signed job manifest to the account’s secure Console feed for any scheduled transient job. The manifest includes subprocessor IDs, exact start/end times, and a hashed job run id; manifests are signed with our platform key and persisted for audit. We’ll provide a sample manifest format and enable the feed for CLM-0423 upon onboarding.

2) Escrow/compensating control for >72h emergency: We can offer an encrypted snapshot escrow held in an EU-based escrow (or a US-based escrow if you prefer) — the snapshot remains encrypted under a key you control or under a dual-control HSM arrangement. The snapshot is only accessible under joint-approval (Redwood exec + Claremont exec) while the emergency is in effect. Marissa will draft the brief escrow clause for the DPA addendum.

3) Next steps:
 - Marissa will circulate a one-paragraph DPA addendum capturing the 72-hour threshold, the exec-approval path for >72h, and the escrow/control language.
 - Ops (Kimberly) will enable the account notification feed and share the manifest sample.
 - I will upload the signed runbook and the roster to the Drive folder and send you the DocuSign link for the addendum.

Schedule target: if we execute the addendum this week we can enable pinning and begin ingest within 48 hours.

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the DocuSign link and runbook location.

Sergio Alvarez
Head of North America Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference
